items.question: Where is exchangeCodeForToken defined and what endpoint does it call?
key_facts: exchangeCodeForToken is defined in server/src/features/auth/services/github.service.ts
It POSTs to https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token
It sends client_id, client_secret, code, and redirect_uri
It throws a friendly 'expired or already used' error for expired/invalid/bad_verification_code responses
It returns data.access_token

items.question: Where is the user JWT created, and what claims and expiry does it use?
key_facts: The JWT is created by generateUserJWTToken in jwt.service.ts
The payload contains userId and githubUsername
It is signed with JWT_SECRET
Expiry defaults to 7 days
Expiry can be overridden with the JWT_EXPIRY_SECONDS environment variable

items.question: Where is the text splitter for chunking configured?
key_facts: The splitter is configured in server/src/features/indexing/chunk.service.ts
It uses LangChain's RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
chunkSize is 2000 and chunkOverlap is 400
Only documents whose pageContent is longer than 6000 characters are split; smaller docs are kept whole

items.question: Which function creates the Qdrant collection, and with what vector size and distance?
key_facts: ensureQdrantIndexes in vector.service.ts creates the collection if it does not exist
Vectors are 3072-dimensional (matching text-embedding-3-large)
Distance metric is Cosine
It also creates a keyword payload index on metadata.repoId

items.question: Where is the Cohere reranker used, and how many docs does it keep?
key_facts: The reranker is the rerank node in rag.service.ts
It uses CohereRerank with model rerank-v3.5
topN is min(5, number of retrieved docs)
If COHERE_API_KEY is missing or reranking throws, it returns the original unranked docs

items.question: Where is requireAuth defined, and where does it look for the token?
key_facts: requireAuth is defined in server/src/middleware/authMiddleware.ts
It checks the Authorization: Bearer header first
It falls back to the 'token' cookie
Missing token returns 401; expired token returns 401 'Token expired'; other invalid tokens return 403
On success it attaches the decoded payload to req.user

items.question: Where is the repoId generated from a GitHub URL?
key_facts: generateUniqueRepoId in git.service.ts builds the repoId
It strips the protocol prefix and trailing .git
It replaces runs of non-word characters with underscores
Despite a comment about hashing, no hashing is performed
A duplicate private implementation exists in GitHubApiService

items.question: Where is the structured answer schema defined?
key_facts: The schema is the zod object 'qa' in rag.service.ts
It has an answer string and a citations array
Each citation has file, startLine, endLine, and snippet
It is applied with llm.withStructuredOutput using method jsonSchema and strict: true

items.question: Which React component polls ingestion progress?
key_facts: ProgressBar in client/src/components/auth/promptbaringeststatus.tsx polls progress
It calls getIngestionStatus, which hits GET /index/status/:jobId
It polls every 1000ms with setInterval
It calls onComplete when progress >= 100 or status is 'completed'
It shows 'Worker waking up' when status is 'waiting'

items.question: Where is findOrCreateUser, and what does it update for existing users?
key_facts: findOrCreateUser is in server/src/features/auth/services/user.service.ts
It looks up the user by githubId
New users are created with username, avatarUrl, email (falling back to a users.noreply.github.com address), and accessToken
For existing users it updates and saves accessToken

items.question: How does authentication work?
key_facts: Users log in with GitHub OAuth
The OAuth code is exchanged for a GitHub access token
The GitHub profile is fetched and a Mongo user is found or created
The server issues its own JWT
Tokens are stored in httpOnly cookies (github_access_token, token, installation_id)
requireAuth verifies the JWT on protected routes

items.question: How does the ingestion worker avoid using resources when idle?
key_facts: The BullMQ worker is created lazily by ensureWorker
indexRepo calls ensureWorker before adding a job
After a job completes or fails, scheduleWorkerSleep closes the worker after 15 minutes idle (IDLE_SLEEP_MS)
The Redis client uses lazyConnect so it does not connect at startup

items.question: How does the loader decide what becomes a document?
key_facts: TsmorphCodeLoader uses ts-morph to parse the cloned repo
It globs .ts, .tsx, .js, and .jsx files, ignoring node_modules and dist
Each file becomes one document with its full text
Each function declaration and class declaration becomes its own document
Metadata includes repoId, repo-relative filePath, declarationName, startLine, and endLine
Arrow functions assigned to consts do not get separate documents

items.question: How does retrieval work before the LLM sees code?
key_facts: createCodeRetriever wraps the base retriever in a MultiQueryRetriever
The MultiQueryRetriever uses gpt-4o-mini to generate 3 search queries
The base retriever uses MMR search with k = 8
Results are filtered on metadata.repoId
The retrieve node in rag.service.ts invokes the retriever with the question

items.question: How are different repos kept separate in the vector DB?
key_facts: All repos share a single Qdrant collection (devai_collection_01)
Each document stores repoId in its metadata at ingestion
The retriever filters on metadata.repoId
A keyword payload index on metadata.repoId keeps the filter fast

items.question: How is prompt cost kept bounded?
key_facts: Context is capped at MAX_TOKENS = 6000
Tokens are estimated as characters / 4 (roughTokens)
Docs are appended until the budget would be exceeded
Only the last 30 conversation messages are included
Reranking keeps at most 5 docs

items.question: How does the server stay responsive during cold starts?
key_facts: The server calls app.listen before loading heavy dependencies
Mongo, Qdrant setup, and the index worker load after listen via dynamic imports
rag.service and index.job are lazy-loaded on first use
A /api/keep-alive endpoint keeps the Render service warm
/api/health always returns 200 and reports Mongo state

items.question: How are Qdrant connection failures detected and reported?
key_facts: Errors are classified by code and message string matching (ECONNREFUSED, ETIMEDOUT, 'qdrant', 'fetch failed', 502, 503, etc.)
Logs include a hint that the Qdrant Cloud free tier may be suspended after inactivity
Ingestion batch errors are logged and rethrown so the BullMQ job fails
At query time the retrieve node throws VECTOR_DB_DOWN

items.question: Trace GitHub login through JWT creation.
key_facts: GET /api/auth/github redirects to GitHub OAuth authorize with scope read:org
GitHub redirects back to /api/auth/callback handled by handleGitHubCallback
exchangeCodeForToken swaps the code for an access token
getGitHubUserProfile fetches the GitHub profile
findOrCreateUser upserts the Mongo user
generateUserJWTToken signs a JWT with userId and githubUsername
Cookies are set and the user is redirected to /orgselector or /install-github-app

items.question: Trace a question from the chat input to the SSE response.
key_facts: handleSubmit stores the user message, then calls postUserPrompt
postUserPrompt POSTs to /query/question with url, prompt, type, sessionId
The route is protected by requireAuth and handled by askController
askController sets SSE headers and lazily imports answerQuestion
answerQuestion runs retrieve, rerank, and generate
askController writes answer_chunk, citations, and complete events
The client reads the stream in processStreamingResponse

items.question: Trace how a citation becomes the file shown in the viewer.
key_facts: rag.service normalizes bare filenames in citations to full repo-relative paths using retrieved doc metadata
askController sends citations in an SSE 'citations' event
The client only keeps the first citation's file, lines, and snippet for the message
Clicking the file calls handleFileSelect which sets the selected path
FilePreview calls getRepoFileContent, which hits /auth/github-file-content
getGitHubFileContent proxies the GitHub contents API with the cookie token and base64-decodes the content

items.question: Trace how the repo list is fetched for a selected org.
key_facts: RepoSelector's fetchRepos calls getReposForOrg which hits GET /auth/repos?org=...
listRepos looks up the user's app installations and finds the one whose account login matches the org
getRepositoriesWithMeta gets an installation token (via a GitHub App JWT)
fetchRepositories paginates /installation/repositories 100 per page
fetchCommitInfo adds the default-branch commit sha for each repo
listRepos has a simple circuit breaker (5 failures, 30s reset)

items.question: How does the selected repo's commit SHA flow into the clone?
key_facts: fetchCommitInfo gets the sha of the repo's default branch
handleSelect sends repoUrl and sha via startRepoIngestion to POST /index/ingest
indexRepo adds a BullMQ job with repoUrl and sha
The worker calls cloneRepo(repoUrl, sha)
A non-HEAD sha triggers a full clone plus checkout; HEAD uses a shallow --depth 1 clone
Clones are cached at .cache/repos/<repoId>/<sha>

items.question: Trace the GitHub App installation check after login.
key_facts: getAppInstallations calls GET https://api.github.com/user/installations with the user token
checkIfAppInstalled matches an installation by app_id or app_slug
The installation id is stored in an installation_id cookie
Installed users are redirected to /orgselector, others to /install-github-app

items.question: How does logout clear the session on client and server?
key_facts: The useLogout hook calls logoutUser and then navigates to /login
logoutUser POSTs to /auth/logout with credentials
The server logout handler clears github_access_token, token, and installation_id cookies
The token cookie is cleared with secure: false and sameSite: lax, which does not match how it is set in production (secure, sameSite none)

items.question: How does the frontend know who the current user is?
key_facts: useCurrentUser calls getCurrentUserFromApi on mount
getCurrentUserFromApi fetches GET /auth/me with credentials
getMe verifies the JWT from the token cookie and returns userId and githubUsername only
No token is sent to the client
formatDisplayName turns the GitHub username into a display name

items.question: What happens when the frontend /auth/callback page loads?
key_facts: AuthCallback reads the code query param and calls completeAuth(code)
completeAuth POSTs to /auth/complete
A completeAuth controller exists in auth.controller.ts
auth.routes.ts does not register a /complete route, so the request would 404
The working OAuth path is the server-side GET /api/auth/callback (handleGitHubCallback)

items.question: What calls answerQuestion, and where is its result consumed?
key_facts: askController in query.controller.ts is the only caller
It lazy-loads rag.service with a dynamic import
It reads result.response.answer and result.response.citations
The answer is streamed as answer_chunk events and citations as a citations event
traceUrl, tokens, and latency are returned but not used

items.question: What calls upsert, and what calls those callers?
key_facts: upsert embeds docs and writes them with QdrantVectorStore.fromDocuments
processBatch in the index.job worker calls upsert for batches of 50 docs
Up to 5 batches run concurrently with Promise.all
The worker is created by ensureWorker, which indexRepo calls before queueing a job
index-production.job.ts also calls upsert but is not wired to any route

items.question: Who calls getAppInstallations, and how is the result used?
key_facts: handleGitHubCallback and completeAuth call it to decide whether the app is installed and to set installation_id
getGitHubUserOrgs uses it to find a personal installation and include the personal account
listRepos uses it to find the installation whose account login matches the requested org
It calls GET /user/installations with the user's GitHub token

items.question: What depends on generateUniqueRepoId, and why must ingestion and query agree on it?
key_facts: cloneRepo computes repoId with generateUniqueRepoId and the loader stores it in document metadata
answerQuestion computes repoId from the same repoUrl and passes it to createCodeRetriever
The retriever filters Qdrant on metadata.repoId
If the URL format differs between ingest and query, the filter matches nothing and retrieval returns no docs

items.question: Where is chunkDocuments used?
key_facts: The index.job worker calls chunkDocuments after loading documents
index-production.job.ts also calls it
The test scripts test-full-pipeline.ts and test-github-api.ts call it
vector.service.ts imports chunkDocuments but does not use it

items.question: Where is the Conversation model written and read?
key_facts: askController upserts the user and assistant messages after answering
addMessage (POST /query/store) also stores the user message, which the client calls first
rag.service's generate node pushes the assistant message too, so messages can be duplicated
rag.service reads the conversation by sessionId for history
chatHistory controllers, the usage report, and the training export read conversations

items.question: What calls getInstallationToken, and what does it depend on?
key_facts: getRepositoriesWithMeta in github.service.ts calls getInstallationToken
It depends on generateAppJwt, which signs an RS256 JWT with the GitHub App private key
It POSTs to /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens
A second getInstallationToken exists in githubApp.auth.ts using Octokit createAppAuth, used by githubApp.service getUserRepos

items.question: Which routes use requireAuth, which use requireTeamAuth, and which have neither?
key_facts: Query routes (/question, /store), chat history routes, and usage report routes use requireAuth
Training routes use requireTeamAuth
The index ingest and status routes have no auth middleware
Most auth routes have no middleware and check tokens themselves; only /app/install/callback uses requireAuth

items.question: Where does Qdrant configuration come from?
key_facts: vector.service.ts creates the Qdrant client lazily in getQdrantClient
It uses QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_API_KEY environment variables
dotenv is loaded from src/config/.env relative to the module
The collection name devai_collection_01 is hardcoded

items.question: Which models are used for embeddings, generation, and reranking, and where are they set?
key_facts: Embeddings use OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (set in vector.service.ts)
Answer generation uses gpt-4o-mini at temperature 0 (rag.service.ts)
MultiQuery query generation also uses gpt-4o-mini (vector.service.ts)
Reranking uses Cohere rerank-v3.5 (rag.service.ts)
Keys come from OPENAI_API_KEY and COHERE_API_KEY

items.question: How is the GitHub App private key loaded?
key_facts: config/auth.ts reads GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY and throws if it is missing
Literal \n sequences are replaced with real newlines
github.service.ts uses it to sign the GitHub App JWT
githubApp.auth.ts reads a differently named variable, GITHUB_PRIVATE_KEY

items.question: How are CORS origins configured?
key_facts: app.ts defines a local allowedOrigins list (localhost:5173, dev-ai.app, vercel domains, ngrok)
The cors middleware allows requests with no origin or an allowed origin, with credentials
A second middleware sets CORS headers manually and answers OPTIONS preflight with 200
config/allowedOrigins.ts exists but its import is commented out
Disallowed origins get a 403 from the error handler

items.question: How are auth cookies configured in dev vs production?
key_facts: Cookies are httpOnly with path '/'
In production they are secure with sameSite 'none'; in development sameSite is 'lax' and not secure
maxAge is 7 days
completeAuth always uses secure: true and sameSite: 'none'

items.question: How does the frontend choose its API base URL?
key_facts: API_BASE_URL is defined in client/src/api.ts
It uses VITE_API_BASE_URL if set
Otherwise in production builds it uses https://devai-b2ui.onrender.com/api
Otherwise it is an empty string (relative URLs)

items.question: How is Redis/BullMQ configured for indexing?
key_facts: The connection comes from REDIS_URL
The client uses lazyConnect and maxRetriesPerRequest: null
Retry backoff is min(times * 50, 2000) ms
If REDIS_URL is unset, a localhost client with no retries is created and the worker will not run
The BullMQ queue is named 'index'

items.question: Where does the MongoDB URI come from, and what happens on failure?
key_facts: The URI comes from MONGO_URI
It falls back to mongodb://localhost:27017
connectMongo calls process.exit(1) on connection failure
server.ts logs that the server will continue, but the process actually exits

items.question: How does ingestion start, report progress, and persist vectors?
key_facts: POST /api/index/ingest (indexRepo) ensures the worker is running and adds a BullMQ job, returning jobId
The worker clones the repo, loads docs with TsmorphCodeLoader, and chunks them
Progress is updated to 15 after clone, 30 before chunking, 36 before upserting, then scaled to 100 per batch
Docs are upserted in batches of 50 with 5 batches in parallel
upsert embeds with text-embedding-3-large and writes to Qdrant
The client polls GET /api/index/status/:id (getJobStatus) every second

items.question: Which LangGraph nodes run, in what order, and what state does each add?
key_facts: The graph runs retrieve, then rerank, then generate
The input state has only question
retrieve adds context (retrieved docs)
rerank replaces context with the top reranked docs
generate adds response (structured answer and citations)

items.question: How are answers streamed, and how does the client assemble them?
key_facts: The server sets text/event-stream SSE headers
It sends a status event, then answer_chunk events, then citations, then complete (or error)
The full answer is generated first, then split into 5-word chunks sent every 100ms, so it is not true token streaming
The client reads the body stream, parses 'data: ' lines, and accumulates answer_chunk content
On complete the client stores the answer with the first citation

items.question: How is conversation history stored, used in prompts, and displayed?
key_facts: The client keeps a sessionId in localStorage under documentSessionId
Messages are stored in the Mongo Conversation collection keyed by sessionId, repoUrl, and userId
answerQuestion loads the conversation by sessionId and injects the last 30 messages into the system prompt
The history page calls GET /chat/history/flat, which pairs user and assistant messages with the first citation

items.question: How are prompt types chosen on the client and applied on the server, and do they match?
key_facts: Quick prompt buttons set a prompt type: Find, Bugs, Debug, WalkThrough, Services (default is 'default')
The server picks SYSTEM_PROMPTS[type] and falls back to Find if the key does not exist
The client sends 'WalkThrough' but the server key is 'Walkthrough', so walkthroughs fall back to Find
'default' also falls back to Find
The temperature values in SYSTEM_PROMPTS are never used; the LLM runs at temperature 0

items.question: How is usage tracked, stored, and read?
key_facts: askController calls appendQueryLog after each question
appendQueryLog appends a tab-separated line to server/logs/query-log.txt
buildUsageReport aggregates Conversation and User data into per-user sessions and queries
writeUsageReportToFile writes logs/usage-report.txt
GET /api/usage-report and /api/usage-report/query-log (requireAuth) return the report and log

items.question: How does the fine-tuning pipeline decide readiness, export pairs, and track runs?
key_facts: extractTrainingPairs builds user-to-assistant pairs from the same session in Conversation data
Each pair's instruction includes up to 4 prior messages of context, and citations are appended to the response
checkTrainingReadiness compares the pair count with min_pairs (default 200)
startTrainingRun only uses data newer than the last completed TrainingRun's lastDataTimestamp
TrainingRun documents track status (running/completed/failed), counts, and model version
Training routes are protected by requireTeamAuth
